items.claim: Deals honesty: scheduled nudges are recorded as 'queued' but nothing ever sends them.
items.evidence: app/api/admin/deals/[id]/nudges/route.ts:66-81 inserts a dealNudges row with status='scheduled' whenever sendNow is false and scheduledAt is set, and does nothing else. Grep of app/, lib/, workers/ for `dealNudges` finds zero other references outside this route (no cron/sweep reads status='scheduled'). `find app/api -ipath '*cron*'` lists ~25 cron routes; none mention nudges. The deal timeline is told about it (route.ts:181-185 'Nudge scheduled for ...'), so the UI actively promises a future send that the system can never fulfil.
items.fix: Decide remove-vs-build per the brief. Remove (cheapest, ~0.25d): drop the 'schedule' mode from NudgeDialog (app/(dashboard)/deals/[id]/deal-detail.tsx:2853, 2879-2880) and stop accepting scheduledAt in POST /api/admin/deals/[id]/nudges, leaving only draft/send-now. Build (~1-1.5d): add app/api/admin/cron/send-scheduled-nudges/route.ts that selects dealNudges WHERE status='scheduled' AND scheduledAt<=now, reuses the deliverEmail block already in nudges/route.ts (factor it into lib/deal-nudge-send.ts so both the POST route and the cron call one function), updates status to sent/failed, appends the same logActivity call, and registers in the existing cron registry (app/api/admin/crons/route.ts + wrangler cron trigger, matching the pre-call-digest pattern).
items.tests: Vitest against the fake-D1 harness: a scheduled nudge with scheduledAt in the past is picked up and sent on the next sweep tick; one in the future is left alone; a failed send flips status to 'failed' and records suppressed addresses. If removing instead: a test asserting the API rejects/ignores scheduledAt and the dialog has no schedule affordance.

items.claim: Deals honesty: the 'Auto Nudges: Active/Paused' toggle implies an automation engine that does not exist.
items.evidence: db/schema.ts:2073-2074 defines deals.autoNudgesDisabled as a plain flag. It is read/written only for display and PATCH bookkeeping: app/(dashboard)/deals/deals-content.tsx:1394-1395 and app/(dashboard)/deals/[id]/deal-detail.tsx:823-849 render 'Active'/'Paused' and PATCH it; app/api/admin/deals/[id]/route.ts:443,711-719 persists the flag and logs an 'auto_nudges_toggled' activity. Grep for autoNudgesDisabled repo-wide (excluding those two UI files) turns up only the GET/PATCH plumbing and the MCP tool property (workers/mcp-server/src/index.ts:1084) - no cron, no stalled-deal scan, nothing that ever sends a nudge because this flag is 'Active'.
items.fix: Same remove-vs-build call. Remove (cheapest, ~0.25d): delete the SidebarCard block (deal-detail.tsx:823-850ish) and the badge (deals-content.tsx:1393-1396) until a real engine exists; keep the schema column dormant or drop it. Build (~2d): a cron (app/api/admin/cron/auto-nudge-stalled/route.ts) that finds deals in the Stalled state (or, after MC.6, deals with the stalled flag set) with autoNudgesDisabled=0 and no nudge sent in N days, drafts from a chosen nudge-template (app/api/admin/nudge-templates/route.ts) and calls the same lib/deal-nudge-send.ts helper from T3.8a, with a per-deal cadence guard to avoid double-sends.
items.tests: Vitest: a stalled, auto-nudge-enabled deal untouched for N days gets exactly one nudge per cadence window; a paused deal or one nudged yesterday is skipped; cadence guard is idempotent across repeated cron ticks.

items.claim: Deals honesty: a nudge is marked 'sent' even when RESEND_API_KEY is not configured.
items.evidence: lib/email-delivery.ts:157-163,230-240 - getResend() returns null when process.env.RESEND_API_KEY is unset, and deliverEmail then returns { success: false, error: 'RESEND_API_KEY not configured', delivered: [], blocked: false } without ever calling Resend. app/api/admin/deals/[id]/nudges/route.ts:137-149 checks `if (!outcome.success)`, sets the row's status to 'failed', and returns a non-2xx response with the error - it never writes status='sent' on that path. The suppression-log ordering is also correct: recordEmailSuppressions runs before the API-key check (email-delivery.ts:170-176), so even a key-less environment leaves a provable trail.
items.fix: No backend fix needed. Note for the record: the front end still can't communicate this failure to the user (see T3.8d) - so although the data is honest, a keyless environment currently just leaves the Send Nudge dialog silently stuck with no visible outcome, which is functionally still misleading to the operator even though nothing false was written to the database.
items.tests: lib/__tests__ already has no-resend-bypass.test.ts guarding the single choke point; add one small regression test asserting POST /api/admin/deals/[id]/nudges with sendNow=true and no RESEND_API_KEY returns status 500/'failed' and never inserts status='sent' (guards against a future refactor re-introducing the bug T3.8c fixed).

items.claim: Deals honesty / T3.9 dialog error surfacing: dialog errors on the deal detail page are swallowed instead of shown to the user.
items.evidence: app/(dashboard)/deals/[id]/deal-detail.tsx:2866-2887 (NudgeDialog.handleSend) - `if (res.ok) onSent()` with no else branch, and `catch { /* silent */ }`; a 409 (allowlist block), 400, or 500 from POST /api/admin/deals/[id]/nudges (which T3.8a/c can legitimately return) leaves the dialog exactly as it was, spinner reset, nothing said. Same pattern at :3071-3095 (ActivityFormDialog.handleSubmit). This is not a missing capability in the file: useToast is imported and used at :14,302 and a working error-toast pattern already exists two hundred lines away at :310-313 and :330-333 (`showToast('Failed to archive deal', 'error')`) - it simply was never wired into these two dialogs.
items.fix: Call useToast() inside NudgeDialog and ActivityFormDialog (both are already separate function components in the same 'use client' module, so the hook is legal there). On `!res.ok`, parse `{ error }` from the JSON body and `showToast(msg, 'error')`, keeping the dialog open so the user can retry; on the 409 case in particular, read `suppressedCount` from the nudge response and show a distinct message ('Held back by the email allowlist (n recipients)') rather than a generic failure. On network catch, `showToast('Network error, try again', 'error')` (no em dash per house style). Do the same audit across the rest of deal-detail.tsx's silent catches (ContactLinker :2258,2272; EngagementEditor :2086,2098) at the same time since they share the identical bug shape.
items.tests: Component test (mock fetch returning 409/500) asserting the toast fires with the server's error text and the dialog stays mounted; one Playwright e2e case: open Send Nudge, force a failing response (e.g. target a non-tahi.studio address pre-launch so the allowlist blocks it), assert a visible error and that the dialog is still open for retry.

items.claim: Deals: Stalled should become a flag settable on any stage, not a pipeline stage in its own right.
items.evidence: 'Stalled' is still modelled as a closing pipeline stage in three places: app/(dashboard)/deals/deals-content.tsx:98 (DEFAULT_STAGES fallback, isClosedLost:1, isClosed:1, closedType:'lost'), app/api/admin/pipeline/seed/route.ts:13, and app/api/admin/pipeline/stages/route.ts:16. The auto-nudge toggle is gated on stage identity, not a flag: deal-detail.tsx:824 and deals-content.tsx:1393 both read `deal.stageName === 'Stalled'`. db/schema.ts has no boolean/flag column for this at all - only the stage row.
items.fix: Schema: add `stalledAt TEXT` (or `isStalled INTEGER`) to deals via a new Drizzle migration, following the repo's IF-NOT-EXISTS-safe ALTER convention (see app/api/admin/db/migrate/route.ts's duplicate-column-swallowing pattern). API: extend PATCH /api/admin/deals/[id]/route.ts (parallel to the existing autoNudgesDisabled handling at :443,711-719) to accept/toggle the flag and log a 'deal_stalled_toggled' activity. UI: replace every `deal.stageName === 'Stalled'` check with `!!deal.isStalled` in deals-content.tsx and deal-detail.tsx, add a small flag/badge visible regardless of stage (Kanban card + list row + detail header), and remove 'Stalled' from DEFAULT_STAGES / pipeline/seed / pipeline/stages defaults. Needs a Liam decision on existing deals currently sitting in the 'Stalled' stage: migrate them to isStalled=1 plus back into their prior stage, or leave as-is and let the flag apply going forward only.
items.tests: Vitest: migration idempotency (running twice does not error); PATCH sets/clears isStalled and writes one activity row per transition; DEFAULT_STAGES/seed no longer contain a stage named Stalled. Component test: badge renders on a Discovery-stage deal with isStalled=1. E2e: flag a deal stalled from any kanban column, confirm it stays in its column with a visible flag rather than jumping to a separate column.

items.claim: Deals v3 lap: /deals is still bespoke rather than composed from the shared list-page primitives (FilterBar, DataTable, rail toolbar) used elsewhere.
items.evidence: deals-content.tsx imports only the generic PageHeader, KPIStrip, ViewToggle and Pagination (lines 19-23) but implements its own KanbanView (line 715), DealCard (line 1209) and ListView (line 1409), plus hand-rolled filter state (filterOwner/filterSource/filterValueMin/filterValueMax/showFilters, lines 254-258) instead of components/tahi/filter-bar.tsx's `FilterBar`. Grep confirms only app/(dashboard)/docs/docs-content.tsx, requests/request-list.tsx and tasks/tasks-content.tsx import DataTable/FilterBar/SlideOver, and only clients/, requests/[id]/, invoices/[id]/ and tasks/ import components/tahi/rail's rail-controls/rail-layout (the saved-views/filter rail STATUS.md says Requests and Tasks share) - deals/ appears in none of those import lists.
items.fix: Swap deals-content.tsx's KanbanView/ListView/ad-hoc filters onto the shared primitives: replace the manual filter state with `FilterBar` (components/tahi/filter-bar.tsx) driving owner/source/value-range filters; replace ListView's custom table with `DataTable` (components/tahi/data-table.tsx) for column sort/pagination consistency with Requests/Tasks/Docs; consider moving onto the rail/saved-views layout (components/tahi/rail/rail-controls.tsx, rail-layout.tsx) so Deals gets the same saved-view/filter-chip UX as Requests and Tasks. Keep the Kanban board itself (Requests/Tasks don't have an equivalent to swap in). This is a composition swap, not new backend work.
items.tests: Existing e2e/vitest for /deals list/filter/sort behaviour should be updated to exercise FilterBar/DataTable instead of the bespoke controls; add a visual/dark-mode + 375px pass per Definition of Done since this touches the whole list page chrome.

items.claim: Repo-wide alert()->toast migration: no alert() calls remain anywhere in the app.
items.evidence: grep -rn "alert(" app/ components/ (excluding tests) shows zero remaining in app/(dashboard)/deals/**, but real ones persist elsewhere: app/(dashboard)/content-studio/audits/audits-content.tsx:41,55,66; app/(dashboard)/content-studio/drafts/[id]/round-table/round-table-detail.tsx (9 call sites, lines 218-313); app/(dashboard)/content-studio/site-index/site-index-content.tsx:57,62,64; and, most notably, the CLIENT-FACING public artifact app/p/proposal/[token]/proposal-viewer.tsx:260,275. design-system/design-system-content.tsx has ~15 more but those are the component-gallery demo page's placeholder onClick handlers, not production UX.
items.fix: Deals itself is done. Remaining real fixes: swap the content-studio alert() calls (audits-content.tsx, round-table-detail.tsx, site-index-content.tsx - all internal/admin-only) for the existing useToast pattern. Highest priority: app/p/proposal/[token]/proposal-viewer.tsx:260,275 is a client-facing public page - a raw browser alert() on a public proposal accept/decline flow is the worst possible surface for it; replace with the same toast/inline-error pattern the deliverable kit already uses elsewhere in app/p/. Leave design-system-content.tsx alone (it's a component showcase, not user-facing).
items.tests: Grep-based lint rule or a repo test (like no-resend-bypass.test.ts's pattern) that fails CI if a new `alert(` appears outside design-system-content.tsx, so this doesn't regress silently again.

items.claim: Em-dash/en-dash metadata cleanup: no em dash (—) or en dash (–) remains in code strings/JSX text per CLAUDE.md rule 6.
items.evidence: A scripted scan of app/, components/, lib/ for U+2014 and U+2013 found 1309 matching lines. Concretely, at least 18 page-level `export const metadata = { title: '... — Tahi Dashboard' }` blocks still use an em dash as the separator (e.g. app/(dashboard)/calculator/page.tsx:6, .../financial-reports/page.tsx:6, .../proposals/[id]/page.tsx:6, app/preview/{contract,proposal,schedule}/[id]/page.tsx:6) - this is literally the pattern CLAUDE.md's own example page-structure snippet shows, so it propagated everywhere. Inside the assigned deals surface specifically, app/(dashboard)/deals/deals-content.tsx:970,972,975 has LOST_REASONS option descriptions containing em dashes that are rendered directly in admin-visible JSX (deals-content.tsx:1130 `{opt.description}`) in the close-as-lost dialog.
items.fix: This is bigger than a deals-only fix: the ~18 metadata titles need the em dash replaced with a colon or comma (e.g. 'Financial reports: Tahi Dashboard' or just drop the suffix), which also means updating CLAUDE.md's own canonical example (`title: 'Feature — Tahi Dashboard'`) since every page copied it verbatim. Within this cluster's scope: replace the em dashes in deals-content.tsx:970,972,975 (LOST_REASONS descriptions) with commas or periods. The other ~1250 hits are mostly code comments and non-UI description strings (db/migrate/route.ts migration descriptions, sitemap seed copy) which are lower priority since CLAUDE.md's own rule 6 targets user-visible text primarily, but the rule as written says 'not in strings, comments, or JSX text' with no carve-out, so a full sweep is a separate, larger workstream outside this cluster's file set.
items.tests: A repo-wide test scanning app/, components/, lib/ for the two dash characters (mirroring lib/__tests__/no-resend-bypass.test.ts's tree-walk pattern) so this stops regressing; scope it to fail on new violations rather than the existing backlog if a full sweep isn't done in this pass.

items.claim: /pipeline hrefs cleanup: internal links/pushes should point at /deals directly rather than the old /pipeline path.
items.evidence: grep for '/pipeline' hrefs/pushes finds 7 live call sites still using the old path: app/(dashboard)/clients/[id]/client-detail.tsx:373 (`router.push('/pipeline?new=1&orgId=...')`), app/(dashboard)/clients/[id]/tabs/deals.tsx:75,96, app/(dashboard)/deals/deals-content.tsx:1256,1497 (the /deals page's own Kanban card and list-row Link both point at `/pipeline/${deal.id}` - i.e. Deals links to itself via the old path), app/(dashboard)/proposals/proposals-content.tsx:286, app/(dashboard)/schedules/schedules-content.tsx:214, and app/api/admin/search/route.ts:352 (global search result href). next.config.ts:88-89 has a permanent redirect (`/pipeline` and `/pipeline/:path*` -> `/deals` equivalents) so these don't 404, but every click round-trips through a 308 redirect instead of a direct client-side navigation - worst on deals-content.tsx where the page links to itself through the redirect on every card/row click.
items.fix: Replace all 7 call sites' '/pipeline' with '/deals' directly (mechanical string swap: `/pipeline/${deal.id}` -> `/deals/${deal.id}`, `/pipeline?new=1&orgId=` -> `/deals?new=1&orgId=`). Keep the next.config.ts redirect in place for old bookmarks/external links, per its own stated purpose. No schema/API change.
items.tests: A grep-based regression test (or extend the em-dash/alert tree-walk test to also flag literal '/pipeline' in href/router.push strings outside next.config.ts) so a future page doesn't reintroduce the stale path.

items.claim: On every signature (partial or final) a notifications row is written, an email goes to the studio and the other parties, and a deal activity is written.
items.evidence: app/api/public/contracts/[token]/sign/[signerId]/route.ts:152-196 — when the signature is NOT the last pending signer, contractStatus stays 'partially_signed' and the route does nothing beyond the DB update: no notifications insert, no activities insert, no email of any kind. Only when remaining.length===0 (final signer) does it fire-and-forget lib/contract-fully-signed-emails.ts:sendFullySignedContractEmails via ctx.waitUntil. That function (lib/contract-fully-signed-emails.ts:44-271) does email every signer + the creator (satisfies 'email to studio + other parties', but final-only) — it inserts into schema.auditLog (lines 281-307) but never schema.notifications and never schema.activities. The only schema.activities inserts anywhere in app/api/admin/contracts/** are in app/api/admin/contracts/[id]/route.ts:100-129, fired on dealId link/unlink via PATCH, not on signing. lib/notification-links.ts:33-34 already declares 'contract_sent'/'contract_signed' as valid NotificationEventType values but repo-wide grep for their use as an actual insert returns zero hits — the type exists, nothing dispatches it. lib/notifications.ts:459 (notifyAllAdmins) is an existing reusable helper for exactly this that the sign route never calls.
items.fix: In app/api/public/contracts/[token]/sign/[signerId]/route.ts, after every signature (both partial and final): (1) select dealId, orgId, name from contractDocuments (only status/expiresAt/id are selected today at lines 58-66) and, if dealId is set, insert schema.activities (type 'contract_signed' or 'contract_partially_signed', dealId, title with signer name + contract name, createdById 'system') mirroring the pattern already in app/api/admin/contracts/[id]/route.ts:104-129; (2) call lib/notifications.ts's notifyAllAdmins(database, { eventType: 'contract_signed'|'contract_partially_signed', title, body, entityType: 'contract', entityId: doc.id }) so the studio gets an in-app notification on every signature, not just the last one; (3) for partial signatures, also send a lightweight 'X of Y signed' email to the studio (new small helper alongside sendFullySignedContractEmails, or extend it with a partial-signed variant) since today only the final signature emails anyone.
items.tests: vitest on the sign route: assert schema.notifications gets a row and schema.activities gets a row (when dealId present) on both a partial and the final signature; assert the partial-signature branch now attempts an email send (mock deliverEmail).

items.claim: The signed PDF is never stored: no signedStorageKey persistence to R2, no download button, no admin resend action.
items.evidence: db/schema.ts:2908 defines `signedStorageKey: text('signed_storage_key')` on contractDocuments (column exists). Repo-wide grep for signedStorageKey/signed_storage_key outside schema.ts only turns up the migration DDL (app/api/admin/db/migrate/route.ts:548) and a comment in lib/contract-fully-signed-emails.ts:39 ('if contracts.signed_storage_key ever gets reused as a...marker') — nothing ever writes to the column. lib/contract-fully-signed-emails.ts:170-198 builds the PDF via buildSignedPdfBase64 purely in memory and only attaches it to the outbound email (lines 236-244); lib/contract-signed-pdf.ts has no R2/bucket reference at all. app/(dashboard)/contracts/[id]/contract-detail.tsx has zero 'PDF'/'Download' occurrences (grep). app/p/contract/[token]/contract-viewer.tsx has zero 'Download'/'signed-pdf' occurrences; emails/contract-fully-signed.tsx:114 only links back to the public viewer ('View signed contract'), not a PDF. The only 'resend' action in contract-detail.tsx (resendSigner, lines 262-275) hits POST /api/admin/contracts/[id]/email, which resends the pre-sign 'please sign' invite (ContractSignEmail) — there is no action anywhere to resend the fully-signed PDF/covering email after the fact.
items.fix: lib/contract-fully-signed-emails.ts: after buildSignedPdfBase64 succeeds, upload with `(await getCloudflareContext({async:true})).env.STORAGE.put(key, bytes, { httpMetadata: { contentType: 'application/pdf' } })` (same pattern as lib/blog-cover.ts:170-186 uploadCoverToR2), key e.g. `contracts/${contractId}/signed.pdf`, then `database.update(schema.contractDocuments).set({ signedStorageKey: key })`. Add app/api/admin/contracts/[id]/signed-pdf/route.ts: GET streams the R2 object (gated by requireContractAccess) with Content-Disposition attachment, regenerating the PDF on the fly from bodyHtml+signatures if signedStorageKey is empty (covers pre-fix rows); POST re-triggers sendFullySignedContractEmails for a resend. contract-detail.tsx: add a 'Download signed PDF' button (visible when status==='signed') and a distinct 'Resend signed PDF' action next to the existing signing-invite Resend button. Surface the same download link in app/p/contract/[token]/contract-viewer.tsx's fully-signed state for the signers.
items.tests: vitest: mock R2Bucket, assert put() is called with the expected key and signedStorageKey is persisted on the contractDocuments row; vitest for the new GET route's org/contract-scope gate; Playwright: sign a contract to completion, then verify a Download button appears and returns a PDF.

items.claim: Tamper anchor: bodyHtml is hashed into the signature chain, body PATCH is blocked after draft, revoke resets a partially signed contract.
items.evidence: Hash chain: app/api/public/contracts/[token]/sign/[signerId]/route.ts:104-111 computes `chainHash = sha256Hex(`${prevChainHash}|${signerId}|${sigUrl}|${now}`)`. The `doc` select at lines 58-66 only pulls id/status/expiresAt — bodyHtml is never read or folded into the hash, so editing bodyHtml after signatures exist does not break the chain. PATCH gate: app/api/admin/contracts/[id]/route.ts:65-73 selects only orgId/dealId/name into `current` (no status), and line 90 `if (body.bodyHtml !== undefined) updates.bodyHtml = body.bodyHtml` applies unconditionally regardless of contract status — bodyHtml can be edited on a 'sent', 'partially_signed', or 'signed' contract with no guard. Revoke: app/api/admin/contracts/[id]/send/route.ts DELETE (lines 72-88) only resets contractDocuments.publicShareToken/publicSharedAt/status='draft'/sentAt=null; it never touches contractSigners (rows that already signed keep status:'signed' and signatureId) or contractSignatures (rows persist), nor clears finalHash. The UI's own delete-confirm copy at app/(dashboard)/contracts/[id]/contract-detail.tsx:757 ('If signing is in progress, consider Revoke instead') implies Revoke is meant to reset partial progress, but the handler does not do that — a re-shared, revoked contract silently keeps stale prior signatures chained under a document that now reads 'draft'.
items.fix: Hash chain: select bodyHtml alongside status/expiresAt in the sign route and fold `sha256Hex(doc.bodyHtml)` into the chain input for every signature, e.g. `chainHash = sha256Hex(`${prevChainHash}|${signerId}|${sigUrl}|${now}|${bodyHash}`)`, so any bodyHtml drift after the first signature is detectable by recomputing the chain. Note this is forward-only: existing signed contracts' finalHash cannot retroactively include a bodyHtml hash, call that out rather than silently claim full coverage. PATCH gate: select `status` in `current` at app/api/admin/contracts/[id]/route.ts and 400 on any bodyHtml/variableValues change when `current.status !== 'draft'`. Revoke: in the DELETE handler, additionally reset every non-'pending' contractSigners row to status:'pending' (clear signedAt/signatureId), delete the contract's contractSignatures rows, and clear finalHash/signedAt on contractDocuments; log the discarded signature ids to auditLog for a forensic trail since the rows themselves are gone.
items.tests: vitest: (1) sign twice, then mutate bodyHtml directly in DB and assert a recomputed/verification hash diverges; (2) PATCH bodyHtml on a 'sent' contract returns 400, and still succeeds on 'draft'; (3) revoke a contract with 1-of-2 signers signed, then GET the contract and assert both signers are 'pending' and contractSignatures is empty for that contract.

items.claim: The /p/contract public viewer is the only viewer not on the deliverable kit.
items.evidence: app/p/proposal/[token]/proposal-viewer.tsx:31-34 and app/p/schedule/[token]/schedule-viewer.tsx:19-22 both import `{ BrandMark, CoverPage, PageChrome, AccentTitle, BRAND, ... }` from `@/components/tahi/deliverable` (components/tahi/deliverable/index.tsx, 697 lines, exporting BRAND/AccentTitle/BrandMark/PageChrome/CoverPage/SectionHeader/RiskCards/Callout/LegendBar — the shared kit). app/p/contract/[token]/contract-viewer.tsx has zero import from '@/components/tahi/deliverable' (grep confirmed); it instead defines a duplicate local BRAND const (lines 31-59), its own local useInView hook, and its own cover/section markup by hand. Its last substantive rewrite was commit 1876d74f 'premium brand-glass redesign matching proposal deck' (2026-05-07) — a hand-matched visual pass that predates the kit's extraction and both other viewers' subsequent restructuring onto it (proposal-viewer.tsx's own docstring: 'Restructured 2026-05-27...mirroring the schedule viewer's visual rhythm' via PageChrome). It's also the only one of the three missing useSectionDwellTracking (present in both proposal-viewer.tsx:29 and schedule-viewer.tsx:24, absent from contract-viewer.tsx), so admin ShareAnalyticsCard has no dwell data for contracts either.
items.fix: Port app/p/contract/[token]/contract-viewer.tsx (1433 lines) onto components/tahi/deliverable: replace the local BRAND/LEAF/useInView/cover markup with CoverPage + BrandMark + AccentTitle for the hero, wrap each content block (contract bodyHtml, signer roster, signature pad, thank-you state) in PageChrome the way section-blocks.tsx does for proposal sections, and add useSectionDwellTracking alongside the existing useShareViewTracking so contract views get the same analytics as proposals/schedules. Keep the signature pad + hash-chain POST logic unchanged; this is a shell/chrome port, not a signing-logic rewrite.
items.tests: Playwright: /p/contract/[token] at desktop, 375px, and dark rendered and visually compared against /p/proposal/[token] for shared chrome (cover, page sections); vitest asserting ContractViewer renders CoverPage/PageChrome/BrandMark (component presence) rather than the old bespoke markup.

items.claim: Client-detail Contracts tab reads a data shape (expiryDate, storageKey) that the API route does not return.
items.evidence: app/(dashboard)/clients/[id]/tabs/papers.tsx:1-16 docstring explicitly documents and fixes exactly this: 'the expiry column read `expiryDate`; the route returns `expiresAt`...the Download link read `storageKey`, which is not on this response'. The current ContractRow interface (papers.tsx:29-40) and the Expires column (papers.tsx:167-184) both key off `expiresAt`, matching app/api/admin/contracts/route.ts:63 which selects `expiresAt: schema.contractDocuments.expiresAt`. No storageKey-based download link remains anywhere in papers.tsx (grep for 'Download'/'storageKey' in the file is empty); rows now navigate to `/contracts/[id]` (papers.tsx:365-375), which owns the document's own actions. Wired in via app/(dashboard)/clients/[id]/client-detail.tsx:58,423-424 (`PapersTab`), and there is no orphaned old Contracts-tab file left under app/(dashboard)/clients/[id]. Landed in commit b9b47cbd ('feat(clients): rebuild the client detail around nine tabs and a Needs-you strip', 2026-09-06), after the 2026-08-18 audit date.

items.claim: The signature canvas does not survive a mobile device rotation correctly.
items.evidence: app/p/contract/[token]/contract-viewer.tsx:745-760 sizes the canvas bitmap exactly once, in a `useEffect(() => {...}, [])` with an empty dependency array: it reads `canvas.getBoundingClientRect()` at mount, sets `canvas.width/height = rect.width/height * dpr`, and calls `ctx.scale(dpr, dpr)` — there is no resize/orientationchange/ResizeObserver listener anywhere in the file (grep for 'resize'/'orientationchange' returns nothing). The parent shell `padShell` (line 1332-1342) sizes to `height: clamp(11rem, 32vw, 14rem)` — a viewport-width-relative unit — while the canvas element itself is styled `width:100%, height:100%` (padCanvas, line 1344-1349). On a portrait-to-landscape rotation the CSS box resizes (vw changes sharply) but the canvas's internal pixel buffer and the dpr scale factor stay fixed at the old rect from mount, so the drawing surface is stretched by the browser and pointerPos (line 762-767, which uses a fresh getBoundingClientRect() every event) maps future strokes to the wrong bitmap coordinates relative to any ink already drawn.
items.fix: In the sizing effect, add a ResizeObserver on the canvas element (fires on both explicit resize and viewport-driven CSS size changes like vw-based rotation) that recomputes dpr/rect and reapplies canvas.width/height + ctx.scale on every change. Since resizing a canvas destructively clears its bitmap, on resize also reset `hasInk` to false and show a brief toast ('Screen size changed — please redraw your signature') rather than silently discarding ink, reusing the existing showToast pattern already used elsewhere in the codebase (e.g. app/(dashboard)/contracts/[id]/contract-detail.tsx:270).
items.tests: Playwright: open the sign page at 375x812, draw a stroke, resize the viewport to 812x375 (simulating rotation), assert the canvas's width/height attributes are recomputed to match the new getBoundingClientRect()*dpr, and that a fresh stroke after resize submits and produces an undistorted, correctly-aligned signature.

items.claim: Schedules half: share POST snapshots the first published version, email POST rejects unpublished, revoke clears the snapshot (CT.F: 'schedule share writes the first published snapshot').
items.evidence: app/api/admin/schedules/[id]/share/route.ts:44-91: POST reads existing.publishedSnapshot; if null it calls buildSnapshot() and writes publishedSnapshot+publishedAt in the SAME update as minting/refreshing the token (lines 66-90). It never overwrites an existing snapshot (comment lines 63-65) — matches CT.F exactly. app/api/public/schedules/[token]/route.ts:49-56: 404s unless status==='shared', then serves publishedSnapshot when present, falling back to live tables only when publishedSnapshot is null ('back-compat with schedules created before migration 0054'). DELETE share/route.ts:182-192 clears publicShareToken, publicSharedAt, publishedSnapshot, publishedAt and resets status to 'draft' — revoke-clears is fully true. BUT app/api/admin/schedules/[id]/email/route.ts:59-76 selects only {id, orgId, title, subtitle, targetLaunchDate, token} and rejects solely on `!schedule.token` (line 74-76) — it never checks publishedSnapshot/status, so 'email POST rejects unpublished' is not literally enforced, only 'rejects unshared'. This gap is latent today: .claude/backups/tahi-db-20260906T2140Z.sql:5237-5238 shows two real production project_schedules rows (Giant Group, status='shared', a live public_share_token) with published_snapshot=NULL, i.e. exactly the shared-but-unpublished state the email guard is supposed to catch. A POST to /email on either of those ids today would succeed and hand out a link that still live-falls-through, because nothing has re-invoked POST /share since CT.F shipped to self-heal them.
items.fix: In app/api/admin/schedules/[id]/email/route.ts, select schema.projectSchedules.publishedSnapshot (or .status) alongside .token and return 400 'Publish the schedule first' when publishedSnapshot is null, mirroring the share route's own invariant instead of relying on token presence as a proxy. Optionally add a one-off backfill (or have the email route itself call buildSnapshot-equivalent) to self-heal the two known shared-but-unpublished Giant Group rows so historical links stop live-falling-through.
items.tests: Vitest: POST /api/admin/schedules/[id]/email with a schedule that has a token but publishedSnapshot=null asserts 400; with a published snapshot asserts success. Extend lib/__tests__/email-invoice-proposal-schedule.test.tsx if it already covers this route.

items.claim: Deliverable kit theme integrity: --page-chrome-text is consumed so dark-slide text is visible in both viewers; app/p/layout.tsx pins light tokens so a viewer's dark localStorage cannot corrupt a public document; unwired slide-theme options are hidden.
items.evidence: components/tahi/deliverable/index.tsx:272 sets `['--page-chrome-text' as string]: p.childText` on the PageChrome wrapper, but a repo-wide grep for 'page-chrome-text' (`grep -rn page-chrome-text components app`) returns only that one definition site — zero consumers. components/tahi/schedule-section-renderers.tsx hardcodes text colours regardless of theme: `proseStyle` (line 497-501) is `color: '#1f2c1a'` used by OverviewSection/TextSection html (lines 129, 357), and SlideShell's AccentTitle (line 110) and deliverable/index.tsx's SectionHeader→AccentTitle (line 363) never pass `onDark`, so titles default to BRAND.ink (#1f2c1a) too. When a section's themeMode is 'dark' or 'feature', PageChrome's surface becomes #1f2c1a (paletteForTheme, index.tsx:196-224) — so #1f2c1a text sits on a #1f2c1a background: invisible. Same pattern reproduced verbatim in app/p/proposal/[token]/section-blocks.tsx (hardcoded `color: '#1f2c1a'` at lines 389/393/433/443/1063). Second sub-claim: `find app/p -iname layout*` returns nothing — there is no app/p/layout.tsx anywhere in the tree, so no mechanism pins light tokens for /p/* routes. app/layout.tsx:78-82 unconditionally injects a script that adds `.dark` to <html> from localStorage 'tahi-theme' on EVERY route including /p/schedule, /p/proposal, /p/contract; app/globals.css defines `.dark` overrides for --color-bg-secondary/--color-text-muted/--color-border etc. (used by RiskRegisterSection/RaciMatrixSection table styles via var(--color-...)), so a visitor who previously toggled dark mode in the dashboard on the same origin gets those vars flipped on a public document with no override. Third sub-claim (hide unwired theme options): NOT applicable as originally stated — the 3-way Light/Dark/Feature picker (app/(dashboard)/schedules/[id]/schedule-detail.tsx:1120-1125 ScheduleSlideThemeSegmented, and the parallel SlideThemeSegmented in app/(dashboard)/proposals/[id]/proposal-detail.tsx:1510-1514) IS wired end-to-end (onPatch -> PATCH -> themeMode column -> read by the public route -> passed into PageChrome, which does change background/border per theme), so it is not an inert/unwired control any more; it produces a visible (broken) effect rather than no effect, so there is nothing left to hide for that sub-claim.
items.fix: 1) Make PageChrome children theme-aware: either (a) replace hardcoded `#1f2c1a`/BRAND.ink/BRAND.body colours in schedule-section-renderers.tsx (proseStyle, AccentTitle calls in SlideShell/SectionHeader) and section-blocks.tsx with `var(--page-chrome-text)` reads, or (b) thread the resolved `theme`/`palette` down into SectionRenderer/SlideShell/section-blocks so each renderer picks BRAND.ink vs BRAND.surface explicitly. Also fix RiskRegisterSection/RaciMatrixSection card/table backgrounds (currently hardcoded '#ffffff') so a dark-themed slide doesn't show a white card floating on black. 2) Add app/p/layout.tsx that renders a plain `<div className="light">`-style wrapper or, more robustly, strips the `.dark` class / forces `data-theme=light` on mount for every /p/* route (a small client effect removing `document.documentElement.classList.remove('dark')` on mount, restoring it on unmount only if outside /p, or simplest: give /p/* its own scoped CSS custom-property block that doesn't inherit `.dark` overrides). 3) No action needed for the theme-picker-hiding sub-claim.
items.tests: Playwright: open a shared schedule/proposal link with 'tahi-theme'='dark' pre-set in localStorage on the same origin, screenshot each of light/dark/feature themed sections, assert no near-black-on-near-black text via a contrast check (or visual regression). Vitest/unit: snapshot PageChrome's rendered style for each theme and assert consumers read var(--page-chrome-text) rather than a hardcoded literal.

'48rem' : '64rem' }}` wrapped only in a single `className="overflow-x-auto"` div (line 111-122) — i.e. still exactly the 64rem pinch-scroll strip described in STATUS.md. items.claim: T3.9 small-fix batch item: global search reads the correct table for schedules and contracts (audit check: 'search reads contract_documents').
items.evidence: app/api/admin/search/route.ts:185-192 queries `schema.contracts` (id/name/status/orgId) for the 'contract' search group — this is the LEGACY table. db/schema.ts:1837 defines `contracts` and the comment at db/schema.ts:2786 explicitly labels it 'the legacy `contracts` table (which tracks file-uploaded PDFs in R2)', superseded by the Phase-3 e-signature system: contract_templates / contract_documents (db/schema.ts:2884) / contract_signers / contract_signatures (db/schema.ts:2782-2811). The schedules half of this claim is fine: search/route.ts:202-208 already queries `schema.projectSchedules`, the one and only schedule table (no legacy duplicate exists for schedules).
items.fix: In app/api/admin/search/route.ts, change the 'contract' group query (lines 185-192) from `schema.contracts` to `schema.contractDocuments` (id/name/status/orgId all exist on contractDocuments too — see db/schema.ts:2884-2922), and update the `href` builder at line ~372 if it assumes the legacy contracts route shape (`/contracts/${r.id}` should already match contract_documents ids used by app/(dashboard)/contracts/[id]). items.evidence: public/proposals/founders-placeholder.jpg is 2,575,793 bytes (~2.46 MB) on disk (confirmed via `ls -la`). It is the default value baked into the proposal 'founders' section (app/(dashboard)/proposals/[id]/section-editors.tsx:154 placeholder text `/proposals/founders-placeholder.jpg`, and app/p/proposal/[token]/section-blocks.tsx:118 sets `image: '/proposals/founders-placeholder.jpg'` as the fallback default). items.fix: Recompress public/proposals/founders-placeholder.jpg to a properly sized/optimised asset (resize to the actual rendered box, ~4:5 aspect, max ~1200px on the long edge; convert to webp/avif with a jpg fallback) targeting well under 200KB. items.claim: Publish-before-share (proposals half): share POST snapshots the proposal, email POST rejects an unpublished proposal, revoke clears the snapshot.
items.evidence: app/api/admin/proposals/[id]/share/route.ts:41-56 (POST) only mints/reuses `publicShareToken` and sets `status:'shared'` — it never calls the snapshot logic that lives in app/api/admin/proposals/[id]/publish/route.ts:30-97. app/api/admin/proposals/[id]/email/route.ts:81-83 only checks `if (!proposal.token)` (i.e. shared) before sending, never checks `publishedSnapshot`/`publishedAt`. app/api/admin/proposals/[id]/share/route.ts:69-75 (DELETE/revoke) clears `publicShareToken`, `publicSharedAt`, sets `status:'draft'`, but never touches `publishedSnapshot`/`publishedAt`. Consequence, confirmed in app/api/public/proposals/[token]/route.ts:50-121: when `publishedSnapshot` is null (true for any proposal that was Shared but never separately Published, e.g. right after first Share) the public GET falls through to live `proposalSections`/`proposalVariants` tables — the standard one-click Share journey still serves LIVE rows exactly as the 2026-08-18 audit found.
items.fix: Extract the snapshot-building block (publish/route.ts:30-88) into a shared helper `snapshotProposal(database, id)` in a new lib/proposal-snapshot.ts. 1) share/route.ts POST: call `snapshotProposal` whenever `publishedSnapshot` is null (first share auto-publishes; a later re-share of already-published content is a no-op) so 'Share' can never leave a proposal in shared-but-unpublished state. 2) email/route.ts: add `if (!proposal.publishedSnapshot) return NextResponse.json({error:'Publish the proposal before emailing the link.'}, {status:400})` alongside the existing token check (needs `publishedSnapshot` added to the select at line 65-79). 3) share/route.ts DELETE: also set `publishedSnapshot: null, publishedAt: null` so a revoked-then-reshared proposal can't silently resurrect stale content without an explicit republish. No schema change needed (columns already exist).
items.tests: Vitest: POST share on a never-published proposal asserts publishedSnapshot is populated afterward; POST email with a token but no publishedSnapshot returns 400; DELETE share clears publishedSnapshot+publishedAt. Playwright: create proposal -> edit content -> Share (one click) -> open /p/proposal/[token] -> confirm content matches at share time -> edit again -> confirm public view unchanged until Publish is clicked.

items.claim: Proposal Publish button dies after the first publish in a session because mutate() doesn't run after every patch/move/delete.
items.evidence: app/(dashboard)/proposals/[id]/proposal-detail.tsx:448-450 computes `hasUnpublished` purely from the local `proposal` state's `updatedAt` vs `publishedAt`. `proposal` is only ever refreshed from the server via the `useEffect` at lines 181-187 that fires when SWR's `swrData` changes, i.e. only when `mutate()` runs. `mutate()` IS called after addSection (240) and addVariant (323), and ONLY in the catch/failure branch of deleteSection (271), moveSection (305) and deleteVariant (344) — never on their success path, and never at all in patchSection (245-265) or patchVariant (328-338), which are the handlers used for ordinary content/pricing edits (autosave on blur). handlePublish (354-367) sets `proposal.publishedAt` locally but nothing subsequently bumps `proposal.updatedAt` locally. Server-side, proposals.updatedAt genuinely IS bumped on every section/variant write (app/api/admin/proposals/[id]/sections/[sectionId]/route.ts:45,61 and .../variants/[variantId]/route.ts:49,65), so the data is correct — the client just never re-reads it after the first publish, so `hasUnpublished` stays false and the button disappears even though real unpublished edits exist.
items.fix: In proposal-detail.tsx, after every successful patchSection/patchVariant call and after the success path of deleteSection/moveSection/deleteVariant, either call `await mutate()` or (cheaper, no round trip) optimistically set `setProposal(prev => prev ? { ...prev, updatedAt: new Date().toISOString() } : prev)` immediately alongside the existing optimistic section/variant state updates. Simplest single-point fix: add the same optimistic updatedAt bump inside `patchProposal` too (currently also missing it) and inside patchSection/patchVariant/deleteSection/moveSection/deleteVariant on their success paths.
items.tests: Vitest/RTL on proposal-detail.tsx: mock the section PATCH endpoint, call patchSection after a prior handlePublish, assert hasUnpublished (via the rendered Publish button) becomes true again. Playwright: publish once, edit a section's text, assert the Publish button/'Unpublished' pill reappears without a page reload.

items.claim: Proposal accept/decline/question closes the loop: notifications row written, Resend email sent to the studio, deal activity written or stage bumped.
items.evidence: app/api/public/proposals/[token]/accept/route.ts (the entire POST handler, lines 33-131) only inserts into `schema.proposalAcceptances` (98-113) and updates `schema.proposals.status` (117-128). There is no call to `createNotifications`/`notifyAllAdmins` (lib/notifications.ts) anywhere in this file, no `deliverEmail`/`render` call, and no insert into `schema.activities`. Repo-wide, `emitDomainEvent(` is only called from app/api/admin/crons/sweep/route.ts and app/api/webhooks/xero/route.ts (confirmed via grep across app/lib) — proposals never emit a domain event either, so no automation/notification path fires indirectly. The public viewer's own copy confirms the promise is unmet: app/p/proposal/[token]/proposal-viewer.tsx:512 'We'll be in touch within one business day', :515/:805 'Liam replies within one business day' — nobody on the studio side is actually told anything happened.
items.fix: In app/api/public/proposals/[token]/accept/route.ts: (1) extend the initial select (67-71) to also pull `dealId, orgId, title`. (2) After the status update block (117-128), call `notifyAllAdmins(database, { type: status==='accepted' ? 'proposal_signed' : status==='declined' ? 'proposal_declined' : 'proposal_question', title: `Proposal ${status}: ${proposal.title}`, entityType: 'proposal', entityId: proposal.id, email: studioProposalDecisionEmailPlan({ proposalId: proposal.id, proposalTitle: proposal.title, status, acceptorName: body.acceptorName, comment: body.comment }) })`. Add 'proposal_declined' and 'proposal_question' to `NotificationEventType` in lib/notification-links.ts:15-50 ('proposal_signed' already exists there, reuse for accepted). Add a new `studioProposalDecisionEmailPlan` builder + React Email template in lib/notification-email.ts (mirror the existing `studioNewRequestEmailPlan` at lib/notification-email.ts:712-738) so a real Resend email reaches the studio, not just a bell row. (3) If `proposal.dealId` is set, insert into `schema.activities` (pattern at app/api/admin/proposals/[id]/route.ts:141-165: `type:'proposal_accepted'|'proposal_declined'|'proposal_question'`, `dealId: proposal.dealId`, `createdById: 'system'` — the existing 'system' sentinel used for unauthenticated writers, confirmed as valid at app/api/admin/proposals/[id]/route.ts:139,147,160) and optionally PATCH the deal's stage on acceptance.
items.tests: Vitest for the accept route: assert schema.notifications gets a row after accept/decline/question (query via test DB), assert deliverEmail/render is invoked (mock lib/notification-email + lib/email-delivery), assert schema.activities gets a row when dealId is set. Playwright (feeds T3.QA): share -> publish -> accept as a client in one tab -> confirm a notification appears for the admin session in another tab/reload.

items.claim: T3.9 sub-item: accept validates against the snapshot rather than live rows.
items.evidence: app/api/public/proposals/[token]/accept/route.ts:78-88 validates `body.variantId` against the LIVE `schema.proposalVariants` table (`eq(schema.proposalVariants.id, body.variantId), eq(schema.proposalVariants.proposalId, proposal.id)`), not against the variant list embedded in `proposal.publishedSnapshot`. If an admin edits a variant's price/scope after publishing (server bumps proposals.updatedAt but the client is still looking at the old snapshot per T3.1/T3.2), the client's accept POST still succeeds because the variantId row still exists live — `decidedVariantId` gets recorded against a variant whose current live data no longer matches what the client actually saw and agreed to.
items.fix: In accept/route.ts, before validating variantId, load `proposal.publishedSnapshot` (add to the select at 67-71) and check `body.variantId` exists in `JSON.parse(snapshot).variants` (matching by id) rather than querying live `proposalVariants`. On accept, also copy the exact snapshot variant's amounts/currency into `proposalAcceptances` (e.g. new columns `acceptedAmountOneOff`/`acceptedAmountMonthly` via an IF NOT EXISTS migration) so the accepted price is frozen even if the live variant is edited/deleted afterward.
items.tests: Vitest: publish a proposal, then PATCH a variant's price live, then POST accept with the old variantId — assert it succeeds and the recorded/returned price matches the snapshot's price, not the live (edited) price.

items.claim: T3.9 sub-item: expiresAt enforcement.
items.evidence: `expiresAt` is only read and displayed, never enforced. app/api/public/proposals/[token]/route.ts:29,71 carries the field through to the viewer as data. app/api/public/proposals/[token]/accept/route.ts never references `expiresAt` at all — an accept POST succeeds on a proposal whose expiresAt is in the past as long as status is still 'shared'. Contrast with the sibling contract flow, which does enforce it: app/api/public/contracts/[token]/sign/[signerId]/route.ts:74-79 rejects with 410 and flips status to 'expired' when `doc.expiresAt` is past.
items.fix: Mirror the contract pattern in app/api/public/proposals/[token]/accept/route.ts: after loading `proposal` (67-71, add `expiresAt` to the select), if `proposal.expiresAt && new Date(proposal.expiresAt).getTime() < Date.now()`, update status to 'expired' and return 410 'This proposal has expired.' before the variant/decision logic. Also add the same check to the GET in app/api/public/proposals/[token]/route.ts so the viewer can show an expired banner instead of live accept/decline buttons on an already-past-expiry proposal.
items.tests: Vitest: proposal with expiresAt in the past -> GET returns an expired flag/state; POST accept returns 410 and flips status to 'expired'. Playwright: set expiresAt to yesterday via admin, load the public link, confirm accept/decline controls are replaced with an expired message.

items.claim: T3.9 sub-item: EmailShareModal preselect.
items.evidence: components/tahi/email-share-modal.tsx:55-57 initializes `selected` via a lazy `useState(() => new Set(suggestions.map(s => s.id ?? s.email)))`, which only runs once at the component's first mount. app/(dashboard)/proposals/[id]/proposal-detail.tsx:713 `onEmail={() => { void ensureContacts(); setShowEmail(true) }}` fires the async contacts fetch and opens the modal in the same tick; `<EmailShareModal>` is unconditionally present in the JSX (proposal-detail.tsx:718, only early-returns null internally when `!open`), so it is mounted once, early, well before `contacts` (and therefore `suggestions`) is populated. By the time `ensureContacts()` resolves and `contacts` updates, `selected`'s one-time initializer has already run against an empty `suggestions` array, so the checkboxes render unchecked even though the intent (line 55-57) is to preselect every suggested contact.
items.fix: Give `EmailShareModal` a `key` derived from something that changes per-open-with-data (e.g. `key={contacts.map(c=>c.id).join(',')}` or `key={showEmail ? 'open' : 'closed'}` combined with contacts loaded), so React remounts it (and re-runs the lazy initializer) once real suggestions exist; simplest robust fix: add a `useEffect` in EmailShareModal keyed on `open` that resets `selected` to `new Set(suggestions.map(...))` whenever `open` flips true (mirrors PromptDialog's own `useEffect(() => { if (open) setValue(defaultValue) }, [open, defaultValue])` pattern at components/tahi/prompt-dialog.tsx:51-57). Alternatively, await `ensureContacts()` before calling `setShowEmail(true)` so suggestions are ready at mount.
items.tests: RTL: render EmailShareModal with suggestions arriving after a delay (simulate the real ensureContacts race), assert all suggestion checkboxes are checked once suggestions land. Playwright: open a proposal with contacts, click Email, assert existing contacts show pre-checked without manual clicking.

items.claim: T3.9 sub-item: save-as-template 400.
items.evidence: app/api/admin/proposals/templates/route.ts POST (33-122) only 400s on `!body.name?.trim()` (46) or when neither `fromProposalId` nor `snapshot` is supplied (103-107). The current caller, app/(dashboard)/proposals/[id]/proposal-detail.tsx:402-418 `saveAsTemplate`, always sends both `name` and `fromProposalId: proposalId`. The PromptDialog that supplies the name (components/tahi/prompt-dialog.tsx:51-57) resets `value` to `defaultValue` (the proposal's title) in a `useEffect` keyed on `open`, so the field is never stale/empty when the dialog opens — the stale-closure class of bug that likely caused the original 400 (per commit 3a8211ba 'fix(sprint-a): ... prompt+confirm modals') appears to already be fixed there. Could not reproduce a 400 against the current code path.
items.fix: No code change identified as needed; if Liam can still repro a 400 in the live app, capture the exact response body (it will be 'name required' or 'fromProposalId or snapshot required') to pinpoint which branch is firing — that would point to a stale client bundle or a different entry point (e.g. MCP create) rather than this route.
items.tests: Vitest for POST /api/admin/proposals/templates: valid name+fromProposalId returns 201; missing name returns 400 'name required'; neither field returns 400 'fromProposalId or snapshot required'. Add a Playwright check: open a real proposal, click Save as template, confirm with the prefilled name, assert 201/success toast, not 400.

items.claim: T3.9 sub-item: alert() to toast.
items.evidence: app/p/proposal/[token]/proposal-viewer.tsx:260 `alert(errData.error ?? 'Failed to submit. Please try again.')` and :275 `alert('Network error. Please try again.')` — both raw browser alert() calls fire when a public (client-facing) accept/decline/question submission fails. No alert() calls remain in the admin dashboard's proposals folder (app/(dashboard)/proposals) — the client-facing public viewer is where the un-styled browser alert survives. There is no ToastProvider mounted for /p routes (no app/p/layout.tsx exists yet; components/tahi/toast.tsx is the shared component but isn't wired into the public tree).
items.fix: Add a small local inline toast/banner state to proposal-viewer.tsx (does not need to wait on the shared ToastProvider or the not-yet-built app/p/layout.tsx from T3.4): e.g. `const [errorBanner, setErrorBanner] = useState<string|null>(null)`, replace both alert() calls at lines 260 and 275 with `setErrorBanner(...)`, and render a dismissible inline error banner near the decision form using the existing design tokens (`--color-danger`/`--color-danger-bg`).
items.tests: RTL/Playwright: force the accept POST to fail (mock 500 or network error), assert an inline error banner renders and no window.alert is invoked (spy on window.alert and assert not called).

items.claim: T3.9 sub-item: /pipeline hrefs.
items.evidence: app/(dashboard)/proposals/proposals-content.tsx:286 links a proposal's linked deal via `href={`/pipeline/${r.dealId}`}`. There is no `/pipeline` route in the app tree — deals live at `app/(dashboard)/deals/[id]` (confirmed via `find`), so every 'Deal' cell link in the proposals list 404s.
items.fix: Change app/(dashboard)/proposals/proposals-content.tsx:286 to `href={`/deals/${r.dealId}`}`.
items.tests: Playwright: from /proposals, click a row's linked deal chip, assert navigation lands on /deals/[id] (200), not a 404.

items.claim: T3.9 sub-item: public tab titles and OG.
items.evidence: app/p/proposal/[token]/page.tsx:3-6 exports a static `metadata = { title: 'Proposal', robots: { index:false, follow:false } }` with no `openGraph` block at all, and no `generateMetadata` function that could personalize it per-token. Grep of app/p/proposal/[token]/page.tsx and proposal-viewer.tsx for `document.title`/`openGraph`/`og:title` returns nothing — every shared proposal link shows the generic browser tab title 'Proposal' and has no Open Graph image/description, so pasting the link into Slack/iMessage/email previews renders a blank/generic card instead of the client's proposal title.
items.fix: Convert app/p/proposal/[token]/page.tsx to use `export async function generateMetadata({ params }) { const { token } = await params; /* fetch title via a lightweight server-side lookup (reuse the same D1 query as the GET route, or call it internally) */ return { title: `${proposal.title} — Tahi Studio`, robots: {index:false, follow:false}, openGraph: { title: proposal.title, description: proposal.subtitle ?? 'A proposal from Tahi Studio', images: ['/og-default.png'] } } }`. Keep the noindex/nofollow robots directive (these are unlisted client-only links) but add real per-proposal title + OG so link previews look intentional.
items.tests: Playwright: navigate to a real /p/proposal/[token], assert document.title includes the proposal's actual title (not the literal string 'Proposal'), and assert an `og:title` meta tag is present with the proposal title.
